title: Slice Resampling, Cost-Fairness and Tenant Prioritization Manual
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document describes the operational procedure, algorithmic policy, and runbook for slice resampling across Redwood's evaluation portfolio with explicit cost, fairness, and tenant-prioritization safeguards. It is intended for evaluation engineers, steward teams who curate probe slices, and SRE/product partners who sign off on budget allocations.

Scope
- Applies to long-running probe rotations and ad-hoc resampling for: shadow evaluations, continuous sentinel probes, and monthly benchmark sweeps.
- Covers integration points with the eval harness (probe scheduler), annotation pipelines, and quantized-artifact gates.
- Does not replace per-model promotion checklists (see model-onboarding docs).

Definitions
- Slice: a labeled subset of prompts representing a workload slice (user intent, language, long-context, etc.).
- Resampling: the process of selecting new probes from the candidate corpus to refresh or expand a slice.
- Priority Weight: numerical score (0.1–10.0) indicating importance when allocating probe budget.
- Tenant Fairness: constraints ensuring no single customer or tenant-derived slice consumes excessive annotation or evaluation budget.

Guiding Principles
1) Cost-aware: every resampling operation must be tagged with an expected token/compute budget and approved by the owning steward or budget owner.
2) Representative: sampled probes must reflect production distributions (traffic fingerprint) plus targeted edge cases for robustness.
3) Fair: enforce per-tenant budget ceilings and soft quotas for high-frequency tenants.
4) Traceable: all resampling artifacts (seed lists, sampler config, annotation batches) must be stored with provenance metadata.

Metrics and Signals (what we measure)
- Probe budget consumption (tokens, model-inference-seconds) — expected vs actual. Threshold: 10% deviation alert.
- Effective coverage delta — fraction of new probes that introduce new token-sequences or new intent tags. Target: >= 12% novelty for a refresh.
- Tenant budget share — per-tenant share of probe budget in a window. Soft cap: 20% of monthly probe budget; hard cap: 40%.
- Annotation latency and cost per label. Target: median <= 48 hours; cost target configurable per tier.

Resampling Policy
1) Trigger types
   a) Scheduled refresh: monthly automated refresh for high-impact slices.
   b) Drift-triggered refresh: data-driven trigger when telemetry shows slice-quality drifts (embedding drift > 0.08 or fidelity drop > 5%).
   c) Emergency expansion: on-call or ATO-driven: immediate resampling to capture a new emergent pattern.
2) Budget pre-authorization
   - Each trigger requires an estimated budget: tokens, expected model runtime (seconds), annotation seats.
   - Auto-approve thresholds: budgets under 100k tokens and inferred runtime < 1200s are auto-schedulable. Larger budgets must be routed to the slice steward and cost-owner.
3) Sampling algorithm (default)\   - Step 0: fingerprint target distribution using lightweight telemetry (last 7 days) and compute stratified weights across language, user-intent, and context-length buckets.\   - Step 1: allocate N probes by bucket using proportional allocation with a floor of 3 probes per bucket.\   - Step 2: within each bucket, select candidates via a hybrid strategy: 60% random from production corpus, 30% targeted adversarial generator (anchor-based), 10% human-curated edgecases.\   - Step 3: enforce per-tenant ceiling by capping selection if tenant_count > threshold (see Fairness constraints).
4) Novelty and deduplication\   - Perform exact token-sequence dedupe and fuzzy canonicalization (normalized whitespace, punctuation).\   - Reject candidates with cosine similarity > 0.95 to any probe in the last 180 days unless explicitly flagged as high-priority.

Fairness and Tenant Prioritization Rules
- Soft quota: no tenant may be allocated more than 20% of that slice's probes in a monthly window without explicit stakeholder approval.
- Hard quota: 40% hard cap enforced automatically at sampling time. Violations generate a billing/ops ticket.
- Priority override: Sales or CSM can request higher priority weight for onboarding customers; this requires written approval and a cost offset plan.

Integration with Eval Harness (operational steps)
1) Create a sampler manifest (YAML) and attach to the slice document in Confluence. Example manifest (required fields):

manifest.yaml:
---
slice_id: "intent-similarity-3"
owner: "nlp-probe-steward"
priority_weight: 2.5
budget_tokens: 120000
trigger_type: "drift"
fingerprint_window_days: 7
sampling_strategy:
  distribution: ["language","intent","context_bucket"]
  composition: {random: 0.6, adversarial: 0.3, human: 0.1}
annotation_policy: "tier-1"
---

2) Push manifest to the eval-harness manifest registry: 
   - CLI: redwood-eval-manifest upload --file manifest.yaml --env shadow
   - CI: manifests are validated by the eval-lint job which checks token budget and schema.
3) The eval scheduler will return a plan (probe batch id, expected cost). Approve if within pre-authorization.

Quantization and Artifact Gates
- Quant-compatibility check: any plan that will be exercised against quantized artifacts must pass the quant-stability gate: run the micro-batch coherence test (5 seeds) on quant profile X and require max coherence degradation <= 3%.
- If quant tests fail, route the batch to non-quant baseline and tag probes with a quant-failure flag for downstream triage.

Annotation and Stewardship
- Annotation tiers: tier-0 (automated auto-label), tier-1 (human single-pass), tier-2 (double-review). Default: tier-1.
- Annotator instructions must include: anchor prompt, expected label schema, disagreement resolution policy, redaction requirements, and privacy gating.
- Storage policy: retain raw probes + annotator decisions for 365 days; derived aggregates retained for 5 years.

Rollout and Promotion Checklist (before adding resampled slice to production evals)
1) Manifest in registry + steward signoff.
2) Dry-run of N=50 probes through eval harness using production model variant and quant artifacts.
3) Acceptance criteria:
   - Novelty >= 12%
   - Quant-coherence pass or documented fallback
   - Per-tenant share <= 20%
   - Expected cost within budget variance +/- 10%
4) Push to shadow mesh for 72 hours and capture telemetry.
5) Final sign-off by owner and product QA.

Regression Triaging Runbook (if resample causes a quality regression)
1) First responder: owning steward opens a Regression-Triage ticket with probe-batch-id and diffs.
2) Quick checks (5–15 minutes):
   - Verify dedupe, tokenization, and canonicalization pipeline outputs.
   - Confirm the manifest sampling_strategy matches execution.
   - Check per-tenant caps were enforced.
3) If regression persists: run targeted bisect (binary split) of the new batch: a) first half vs. second half; b) random vs. adversarial subsets.\4) If bisect indicates adversarial generator spike, quarantine that sub-batch and re-run with human-curation augmentation.
5) Communicate: Status update to impacted teams within 2 business hours and ETA for mitigation.

Config Table (Operational Defaults)
| Field | Default | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| priority_weight | 1.0 | Range 0.1–10.0 |
| budget_tokens | 100000 | Override only with approval |
| fingerprint_window_days | 7 | Adjust down to 1 for emergent issues |
| novelty_target_pct | 12% | Minimum novelty threshold |
| per_tenant_soft_cap | 20% | Monthly window |
| per_tenant_hard_cap | 40% | Enforced automatically |

Operational Commands and Diagnostics
- Validate manifest: redwood-eval-manifest lint manifest.yaml
- Preview plan: redwood-eval-manifest preview --manifest manifest.yaml --n 50
- Force-run (on-call only): redwood-eval-manifest run --manifest manifest.yaml --env shadow --force
- Fetch probe provenance: redwood-probe-store fetch --batch-id <id> --format jsonl

Troubleshooting FAQ
Q: My resample exceeded the budget estimate. What now?
A: Open a cost-variance ticket and pause the batch. If overage < 10% the steward can approve retroactively; larger overages require budget owner approval. Update manifest with corrected budget estimate and re-run gating tests.

Q: A single tenant appears in 70% of selected probes after resample.
A: Immediate action: quarantine the batch, rollback the slice, and open a tenant-fairness incident. Investigate data leakage and adjust fingerprint weights.

Q: Quant coherence failures on micro-batch.
A: Route probes to non-quant baseline, add a quant remediation task to the backlog and add the probes to a targeted quant-retest queue.

Appendix: Example Manifest for a Multi-tenant Onboarding Slice
---
slice_id: "onboard-multi-tenant-coldstart"
owner: "onboarding-steward"
priority_weight: 4.0
budget_tokens: 200000
trigger_type: "scheduled"
fingerprint_window_days: 14
sampling_strategy:
  distribution: ["tenant","language","intent"]
  composition: {random: 0.5, curated: 0.4, adversarial: 0.1}
per_tenant_soft_cap: 0.2
per_tenant_hard_cap: 0.4
annotation_policy: "tier-2"
---

End of document.
